import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset provided as a string
data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Initialize the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize relationships between key sleep metrics
# X-axis: Sleep Duration
# Y-axis: Quality of Sleep
# Hue: Stress Level (to see how stress levels correlate with sleep metrics)
# Style: BMI Category (to differentiate points by body mass index)
# Size: Daily Steps (to add another dimension of physical activity)
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Stress Level',
    style='BMI Category',
    size='Daily Steps',
    sizes=(100, 500),  # Adjust the range of marker sizes
    palette='viridis', # Choose a perceptually uniform color palette
    edgecolor='black', # Add a black edge to markers for better visibility
    alpha=0.8
)

# Add labels and title for clarity
plt.title('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by Stress Level, BMI, and Daily Steps', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10 scale)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlapping with data points
plt.legend(title='Metrics', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot as a PNG file
plt.savefig('output.png')
